problem.statement: Mint a least-privilege fine-grained GitHub PAT for a bot machine account that is an outside collaborator on another user's public repository, to open pull requests via API.

approach.summary: Create a fine-grained PAT on the bot account with resource owner set to the bot, expecting the collaborator repository to appear under repository access.
approach.detail: Bot account -> Developer settings -> Fine-grained tokens; intended scope: single repo, Contents RW + Pull requests RW.

failure.point: The collaborator repository never appears in the fine-grained token's repository selector; fine-grained PATs can only access resources owned by the selected resource owner.
failure.evidence: GitHub documentation, 'Managing your personal access tokens', lists as major gaps of fine-grained PATs: contributing to public repos where the user is not a member, and contributing to repositories where the user is an outside or repository collaborator; only classic PATs have write access to public repos not owned by the token holder. Workaround used: classic PAT with public_repo scope, blast radius equivalent because the bot collaborates on exactly one repo.

environment.description: github.com as of 2026-08; bot is a personal account, repo is public under a different personal account.

transferability.notes: Does not apply when the resource owner owns the repo, or for organization repos where the bot is a member and the org has enabled fine-grained PATs. GitHub lists this gap as temporary; re-verify before relying on it.

confidence.notes: Vendor-documented limitation, independently hit in practice.
